name: FluentValidation/FluentValidation
build_modifications: global.json sdk.version changed from 10.0.0 (unavailable) to 8.0.100 (rollForward=latestFeature already present). Two MSBuild property overrides were required at build time, NOT source edits: (1) -p:DebugType=portable — Directory.Build.props sets <DebugType>embedded</DebugType>, which embeds the PDB inside the DLL with no sibling .pdb file at all, so the oracle tool (which reads a separate .pdb) saw 100% no-debug-info until this was overridden; (2) -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=false — the csproj sets ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true for Release config, which triggers deterministic source-path remapping so the PDB's CallerFile values are prefixed '/_/' instead of being the real repo-relative path; overriding this makes CallerFile values resolve directly against the repo root.
build_caveat: About 5.3% of edges with a non-null CallerFile point into src/FluentValidation/obj/.../System.Text.RegularExpressions.Generator/RegexGenerator.g.cs — a Regex source-generator's virtual output file. The PDB records this path but the generator does not persist it to disk (EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles is off), so those specific rows will not resolve to a real file even though NoDebugInfo=false for them. This is a legitimate generated-code category, not a broken build; spot-checks were done on genuine first-party rows instead.
test_detection_rule: naming suffix .Tests / .Tests.Benchmarks; FluentValidation.Tests.csproj references Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk + xunit; all product and test projects live side by side under src/, distinguished by name only (no separate test/ directory)
test_assemblies_note: Built assemblies, not project files. The pin originally listed .csproj paths here, which the runner could never treat as an answer-key input — the with-tests cell was refused for all three repositories until this was corrected on 2026-08-24.
with_tests_cell: unavailable: the test projects target net10.0 and do not build on the pinned SDK 8.0.421 (NETSDK1045). Recorded rather than silently skipped — the cell is missing, not zero.

name: Humanizr/Humanizer
build_modifications: global.json sdk.version changed from 11.0.100-preview.6.26359.118 (unavailable) to 10.0.400 (rollForward=latestFeature and allowPrerelease=true left as-is) — see corpus-patches/Humanizer.patch. Additionally, -f net8.0 alone is not enough: Microsoft.NET.TargetFrameworkInference.targets validates the FULL multi-target list (netstandard2.0;net8.0;net48;net10.0;net11.0) against the installed SDK before framework selection even for a single -f build, and fails NETSDK1045 on the net11.0 entry regardless. Overriding the TargetFrameworks property itself with -p:TargetFrameworks=net8.0 (build_command above) sidesteps that check entirely. Directory.Build.props sets DebugType=embedded by default (same PDB trap as FluentValidation), hence -p:DebugType=portable. LangVersion=preview in Directory.Build.props built cleanly under SDK 10.0.400 with no preview-only C# syntax errors.
build_caveat: This project uses UseArtifactsOutput=true (Arcade-style layout), so build output lands under artifacts/bin/<Project>/<config>_<tfm>/, not the conventional src/<Project>/bin/<config>/<tfm>/ path.
test_detection_rule: projects living under top-level tests/ directory (Humanizer.Tests, Humanizer.Analyzers.Tests.*, Humanizer.SourceGenerators.Tests); product code lives only under src/Humanizer

oracle_probe.spot_check_notes: ArticlePrefixSort.cs:17 verified; artifacts/obj/Humanizer/release_net8.0/Humanizer.Version.cs:29-30 are a legitimate MSBuild ThisAssembly source-generator output (a real file on disk under artifacts/obj/, unlike FluentValidation's virtual regex-generator rows), not a broken build

test_assemblies_note: Humanizer.Tests.csproj's TargetFrameworks list uniquely includes net8.0 alongside net10.0/net11.0/net48 (Windows) even though the product project no longer ships net8.0 as its primary target, and it DOES build for net8.0 with the same TargetFrameworks-override trick as the product project: `dotnet build tests/Humanizer.Tests/Humanizer.Tests.csproj -c Release -p:TargetFrameworks=net8.0 -p:DebugType=portable -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=false` — the DLL lands at artifacts/bin/Humanizer.Tests/release_net8.0/Humanizer.Tests.dll, confirmed present on disk (2026-09-01). The cell is still unmeasurable, for a different reason: this project uses the Arcade UseArtifactsOutput layout, so its built assembly sits under artifacts/bin/Humanizer.Tests/release_net8.0/, never under tests/Humanizer.Tests/ itself — and runner/run.py's unmatched_test_scope_projects (armkit._project_dir + a path-COMPONENT-prefix match) can only ever recognize a test_assemblies entry that lives somewhere under its test_assemblies_projects entry's own directory. No Arcade-output entry can ever satisfy that check, built or not, so listing this project/assembly pair here always trips runner.py's own disagree-refusal (CellNotMeasurable) rather than grading. Fixing that would mean teaching the runner's project-to-assembly matcher about Arcade layouts, a runner change out of this corpus fix's scope — so test_assemblies and test_assemblies_projects are left empty here rather than left mismatched, and the cell is reported honestly as unavailable.
with_tests_cell: unavailable: Humanizer.Tests.dll builds fine for net8.0 (confirmed on disk), but its Arcade-layout output path (artifacts/bin/Humanizer.Tests/release_net8.0/) never sits under its project's own directory (tests/Humanizer.Tests/), which is what runner.py's test_assemblies_projects/test_assemblies coverage check requires to accept a with-tests cell as measurable — see test_assemblies_note. Recorded rather than silently skipped: the cell is missing, not zero.

name: unitystation/unitystation
pinned_ref: develop HEAD of the maintainer's clone at pin time (detached, not a tag)
license_note: AGPL-3.0 is a copyleft licence. This repository stores only the URL, the sha and generated project files that list source file names; no unitystation source is stored or redistributed. See CORPUS_NOTES.md.
build_modifications: None to unitystation source. unitystation .gitignores the Editor-generated .csproj files, so corpus-patches/unitystation/csproj/ carries 36 of them (the Editor's own output for this sha, with the Editor install folder and the Library folder replaced by MSBuild properties UnityEditorPath / UnityLibraryDir, set from env UNITY_EDITOR_PATH / UNITY_LIBRARY_DIR in corpus-patches/unitystation/Directory.Build.props). build.py copies them into UnityProject/ and runs `dotnet build <each>.csproj --no-restore -p:DebugType=portable`. The csproj files say DebugType=full, which writes a Windows PDB the oracle cannot read; portable is required.
build_requires: Unity 6000.2.10f1 installed (UNITY_EDITOR_PATH) and a Library folder of an imported copy of this sha (UNITY_LIBRARY_DIR, default UnityProject/Library): PackageCache (Mirror and other git packages) and ScriptAssemblies are referenced by HintPath.
build_omitted: Four csproj the maintainer's Editor generated for a local analyzer package that is not part of unitystation (AnalizerEditor, AnalizerTest, Drevo.ArchitectureAnalyzer.AI/.SceneBridge), the empty Assembly-CSharp, the two empty FastScriptReload test projects, and FastScriptReload.Editor (a vendored editor plugin whose Roslyn references the Editor resolves by a mechanism not present in the generated csproj; 142 compile errors outside the Editor).
target_frameworks_produced: unity (.NET Standard 2.1 API profile, csproj TargetFrameworkVersion v4.7.1)
test_detection_rule: asmdef projects Tests and playmodetests (sources under UnityProject/Assets/Tests); everything else is the game, its editor tooling and the vendored plugins that are compiled as their own asmdef
scope_note: The arms' source scope is the parent directory of each listed csproj, which for Unity is the whole UnityProject folder (all csproj sit at its root). The without-tests cell then drops files under a directory named Tests, the same path rule as every other repository. Source files of FastScriptReload.Editor are in that scope but in no built assembly, so grep and repowise can emit callers there that the key cannot hold.
